aerometer.name: Aerometer
aerometer.description: Measures the current aerodynamics of the spaceship. Higher means better.
aerometer.notes: Port on the bottom face (facing -y) of a 2 x 2 x 1 plate. No corpus instance is wired, so the port is prefab-only (baked list = renderer); the footprint is corpus-checked.

altimeter.name: Altimeter
altimeter.description: Measures height above sea level. Outputs INF when outside any atmosphere. For proper functioning, it must be mounted outside the ship with an unobstructed view.

atmometer.name: Atmometer
atmometer.description: Measures current atmosphere density. For proper functioning it must be mounted outside the ship with an unobstructed view.

axis_rotometer.name: Axis Rotometer
axis_rotometer.description: Measures the current angular velocity (degrees per second) about its mounted axis.

distance_meter.name: Distance Meter
distance_meter.description: Measures distance to the nearest object up to 1000 meters and outputs the value to the data port.
distance_meter.notes: Unlike most small sensors its output is on the FRONT face (z = d), at x = 1.

inclinometer.name: Inclinometer
inclinometer.description: Measures the difference in degrees between the component's down direction and the gravity direction.
inclinometer.notes: Same body and port layout as the Aerometer (2 x 2 x 1, port facing -y). No corpus instance is wired, so the port is prefab-only; the footprint is corpus-checked.

massmeter.name: Massmeter
massmeter.description: Measures the mass of the spaceship it is mounted on.

rotometer.name: Rotometer
rotometer.description: Measures the current rotation in degrees per second.
rotometer.notes: No "SC_Rotometer" prefab exists in this game build (globalgamemanagers.assets has SC_AxisRotometer and SC_AxisRotometer M only); hash 955ad7bed99d6821 never occurs in the corpus. The Localization rows remain. Its class EPC_SCRotometer is what SC_AxisRotometer uses, so the Axis Rotometer appears to be its in-game replacement: substitute axis_rotometer.

thermometer.name: Thermometer
thermometer.description: Reads the current temperature and sends it to the data port. Make sure to place it on the outside of the spaceship for best results.

thermoscan.name: Thermoscan
thermoscan.description: Measures the temperature of the first object hit by a ray cast up to 1000 meters and outputs the value to the data port.
thermoscan.notes: No corpus instances (newer part). Same prefab layout as the Distance Meter (2 x 1 x 2, output on the front face at x = 1), which is corpus-confirmed; struct from the IL2CPP inheritance chain (EPC_SCThermoscan -> EPC_SpaceshipComponent).

trajectory_curvature_meter.name: Trajectory Curvature Meter
trajectory_curvature_meter.description: Detects the difference in degrees between the spaceship's trajectory and its facing direction. For proper functioning, there must be no obstacles in front of the component.

velocity_meter.name: Velocity Meter
velocity_meter.description: Detects the current speed in meters per second. For proper functioning, there must be no obstacles in front of the component.

_modeButton.meaning: mode button (bool; declared 4 B but 1 B, `_col` follows at 21): 0 = Overall Mode, output = speed |v|; 1 = Directional Mode, output = v . (part +z axis), signed. Decoded from SCTick_VelocityMeter.OwnJob (toggle < 0.5 -> sqrt(vx2+vy2+vz2), else dot with the rotated forward axis). Default 0 = the prefab toggle's initial state. Both values common in the corpus.

velocity_meter.notes: Output on the back face (z = -1); the front (+z) must be unobstructed, and in Directional mode the reading is the velocity along +z. The one overlap is an SC_FrameB with the same origin: a wedge frame (triangular joint faces), so its 8 x 8 x 4 box has free cells.

windmeter.name: Windmeter
windmeter.description: Measures current wind strength outside of spaceship. For proper functioning it must be mounted outside the ship with an unobstructed view.
windmeter.notes: 2 x 2 x 2; output on the back face, lower row (y = 0).

blue_tank.name: Blue Tank
blue_tank.description: Blue alone is providing very small amount of effectivity with no reactivity. Appears as a blue-colored gas.

_actionableValue.meaning: outlet valve opening, f32 0..1 (EPC_Actionable_Valve: 0 = off/closed, 1 = on/open). The valve has no stored initial value, so the in-game default is not known; 1.0 (fully open) is used here. Corpus: blue 0.90-1.00, green 0.096-0.103, i.e. the 90 % blue / 10 % green mix the manual recommends.

blue_tank.notes: 16 x 32 x 16 cells (2 x 4 x 2 m): the size field, not the joint areas (which span only y = 6..25). Checked: the size-field box gives 6 port hits / 0 misses, the joint-area box 0 / 6; frames, tanks and cables sit directly on top of the 32-cell box and line its sides at every height, nothing inside. Fuel pipe joint on the front face at x = 8..9, y = 6..7 (not a cable port).

green_tank.name: Green Tank
green_tank.description: Green is mediocre fuel. Appears as a green-colored gas.

_actionableValue.meaning: outlet valve opening, f32 0..1 (EPC_Actionable_Valve: 0 = off/closed, 1 = on/open). The valve has no stored initial value, so the in-game default is not known; 1.0 (fully open) is used here. Corpus: blue 0.90-1.00, green 0.096-0.103, i.e. the 90 % blue / 10 % green mix the manual recommends.

green_tank.notes: 8 x 24 x 8 cells (1 x 3 x 1 m), same evidence as the Blue Tank (size-field box: 6 hits / 0 misses; joint-area box: 0 / 6; parts stacked directly on the 24-cell top).

red_tank.name: Red Tank
red_tank.description: A highly efficient but very reactive fuel that must be carefully mixed with other fuels and kept under active cooling. The cooler needs a continuous power supply - if power is lost while fuel remains in the tank, it may explode. When properly mixed and cooled, red fuel delivers the best performance.

_actionableValue.meaning: outlet valve opening, f32 0..1 (EPC_Actionable_Valve: 0 = off/closed, 1 = on/open). The valve has no stored initial value, so the in-game default is not known; 1.0 (fully open) is used here. Corpus: blue 0.90-1.00, green 0.096-0.103, i.e. the 90 % blue / 10 % green mix the manual recommends.

red_tank.notes: No corpus instances. 16 x 16 x 16 cells from the size field (the rule the Blue and Green tanks confirm). Class EPC_SCCryotank derives from EPC_SCTank and declares no Blueprint of its own, and its InitializeEntity calls EPC_SCTank.InitializeEntity first, so it saves with the EPC_SCTank struct (the same inheritance rule is corpus-confirmed for FramePipe/FrameWithPorts -> Frame and ZoomCamera/RotationalTelescope -> Camera). Port order from the baked list: fuel (node X), cooling (node Y), power (node P).

long_range_distance_meter.name: Long Range Distance Meter
long_range_distance_meter.description: Measures the distance to the closest object in front of it, with no limitations on range.
long_range_distance_meter.notes: 2 x 2 x 4; both ports on the back face, lower row. The confirmed placements include orientations where local y maps to a negative world axis (13, 14, 17), so the min-corner rule with the full 2-cell height holds. The one overlap is an SC_FrameQuarterD, a corner frame (triangular joint faces) whose 4 x 4 x 4 box has free cells.

magnetometer.name: Magnetometer
magnetometer.description: Measures electromagnetic activity from the Sun. Used to detect and predict incoming solar storms. Make sure at least 70% of the space around it is clear so it can work properly! The indicator shows signal quality: green = above 70%, red = below 70%.
magnetometer.notes: 4 x 8 x 4 mast; both ports face -x (left side), bottom row. In the twin they face +x.

gyro_line.name: Gyro-Line
gyro_line.description: Gyro-Line shows the spaceship’s pitch and roll orientation on the screen.

_rotKnobValue.meaning: orientation knob (SCTypeGyroLine._actionableOrientationKnob), f32; corpus values 0, 0.25, 0.75 (quarter steps). Prefab knob default 0.

_toggle.meaning: on/off switch (bool; declared 4 B but 1 B). Prefab toggle initial state 1 = on.

_degrees.meaning: display range in degrees, byte: 40 / 60 / 90 / 180 (4-step "Degrees" knob; GyroLineDisplayRange). Corpus: 40 (12x), 60, 90.

gyro_line.notes: Port order (baked list): pitch = node X (x = 1), roll = node Y (x = 2), power = node P (x = 0). direction_conflicts = 2 is one twin placement in a scratch blueprint ("Blah") whose pitch and roll are cabled to Data Router 2 outputs (a wiring error); the other network partners are inputs.

space_gps.name: Space GPS
space_gps.description: Used to determine world-space coordinates as distance, longitude, and latitude relative to the center of the universe (the Sun). Make sure at least 60% of the space around it is clear so it can work properly! The indicator shows signal quality: green = above 60%, red = below 60%.
space_gps.notes: Port order (baked list): distance = node X (x = 3), longitude = X (1) (x = 2), latitude = X (2) (x = 1), power = P (x = 0); all on the front face, bottom row.

space_scanner.name: Space Scanner
space_scanner.description: A satellite module for detecting celestial bodies in deep space. It uses a configurable scanning cone to identify planets and large objects, outputting the distance to the nearest detected object. For proper functioning, there must be no obstacles in front of the component.
space_scanner.notes: 4 x 4 x 8; ports on the back face, bottom row: cone (in, x = 1), distance (x = 2), power (x = 3). The one miss and the one power-on-data contact are the same placement in an "Autosave" snapshot (BlueprintsBin) whose cables sit two cells to -x of the ports; the other 19 placements agree.

fuel_analyzer.name: Fuel Analyzer
fuel_analyzer.description: Used to analyze fuel performance and stability.

_knobVal.meaning: input knob, f32 0..1: the value whose fuel performance is estimated when `_mode` = 0. Prefab knob default 0.

_toggle.meaning: on/off switch (bool). Prefab toggle initial state 1 = on.

_mode.meaning: input source (bool): 0 = "Input: Knob" (`_knobVal`), 1 = "Input: Data Port" (port `value`, clamped to 0..1). Decoded from SCTick_FuelAnalyzer.OwnJob (mode toggle < 0.5 -> knob entity, else the data port). Set 1 when the input port is wired. The declared struct is 30 B; bytes 27..29 are padding (corpus shows junk there; write 0).

fuel_analyzer.notes: Port order (baked list): value (in, x = 1, y = 0), performance = node Y (x = 1, y = 1), stability = node X (x = 0, y = 1), power = node P (x = 0, y = 0); all on the front face. Note performance/stability are NOT in node-name order. Also has a fuel-pipe joint on the front face, right half (x = 2..3). Outputs not confirmed by corpus cables (only 5 unique placements); power and input are.

SC_PipeMeter.name: Pipe Meter
SC_PipeMeter.description: Basic fuel pipe used to transport or temporarily store fuel. Safe for fuel stability ≥50%. Analyzes the proportion of components of the current fuel present in the pipe.
SC_PipeMeter.notes: Not a data part: a fuel pipe segment with three indicator bars and no data or power ports (no port children, no baked port list, no Localization port rows). Pipe joints on the -z and +z faces. No mirrored twin prefab exists.

SC_NanopipeMeter.name: Nanopipe Meter
SC_NanopipeMeter.description: Advanced fuel pipe used to transport or temporarily store fuel. Safe for all fuel types. Analyzes the proportion of components of the current fuel present in the pipe.
SC_NanopipeMeter.notes: Nanopipe version of the Pipe Meter: same geometry, no ports, no twin. No corpus instances.

SC_BaobaraInterferencemeter.name: Baobara Interferencemeter
SC_BaobaraInterferencemeter.description: Electronic equipment used to locate the source of interference on Baobara. Displays the distance to the interference source.
SC_BaobaraInterferencemeter.notes: Quest item (Void Watcher objective): a display that shows the distance to the interference source. No data or power ports. No corpus instances.
